title: Grateful Dead Live at Newcastle-Under-Lyme on 1970-05-24
source: MSR > CDR > PC > my edits in Goldwave > CDR > FLAC; patched with unknown MR > cassette > PC; further patched with shnid 6481

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of the Dead’s first European gig, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and punchy Hard‑to‑Handle.
ai_review.review: Both reviewers rave about the superb soundboard mix – clear, balanced and even forgiving of the extra tuning between songs. Musically the show shines with a mesmerizing Dark Star, a high‑energy Hard‑to‑Handle, and strong renditions of The Other One, Good Lovin’ and Rain & Snow, while a few early numbers like Casey Jones fall a bit flat.

ai_rating.rationale: Two detailed reviews give consistently high marks (5 ★ and 4 ★). The performance is praised overall with only minor song‑specific criticisms, and the soundboard recording is described as fabulous.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Fabulous clarity and balance; a few extra tuning edits between tracks are noted but do not detract. Minor festival stage announcements audible, but overall mix is crisp.

poor_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set unfolds at a deliberate early pace, then builds momentum in the second half with fluid transitions (notably into The Other One) and a powerful Dark Star that ties the show together.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is front‑and‑center – a tight groove on Dark Star and an extra burst of energy on Hard‑to‑Handle.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s vocal contributions are highlighted as a sweet, vulnerable touch early in the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir delivers a solid Me and My Uncle and adds strong rhythm/vocal work throughout.
